primary.title: The Iliad
primary.author: Homer
primary.rationale: One of the foundational epics of ancient Greek literature, attributed to Homer. It describes the final weeks of the Trojan War and the personal conflicts of its heroes.

primary.title: The Odyssey
primary.author: Homer
primary.rationale: Another epic poem attributed to Homer, detailing the ten-year journey of the Greek hero Odysseus as he attempts to return home after the Trojan War.

secondary.title: The Cambridge Companion to Homer
secondary.author: Robert Fowler
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive collection of essays by leading scholars covering various aspects of Homeric studies, including the poems, their historical context, and their reception.

secondary.title: Homer: The Odyssey
secondary.author: Jasper Griffin
secondary.rationale: A seminal critical study of Homer's Odyssey, analyzing its structure, themes, and characters.

secondary.title: The Homeric Question
secondary.author: J.B. Hainsworth
secondary.rationale: While published in 1976, this work is a foundational text in the modern scholarly debate about the authorship and composition of the Homeric epics.

suggestions.notes: The exact historical existence and authorship of Homer are subjects of the 'Homeric Question,' a long-standing debate in classical scholarship. The primary sources listed are the epic poems traditionally attributed to him.
